text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein pardons bread rioters and other prisoners. Calls for Prime Minister Kabariti to review bread prices.
- At state dinner with Indonesian President Suharto, king says Middle East peace process needs international support.
- Foreign Ministry publishes numbers of Jordanian passports stolen when embassy driver in Iraq was killed on Monday. Helicopters hunt for driver's killers.
- Turkish foreign minister Ciller says Ankara will supply Jordan with water.
- Kuwait's Interior Minister Mohammad Khaled al-Hamad al-Sabah says hopes for quick return to natural relations with Jordan. Says there is great understanding for Jordan's position over Kuwait.

- Jordan, Turkey agree on creation of regional security cooperation body. Ciller says technical committee formed to discuss water issues; steps taken to increase trade exchange and bilateral cooperation.
- Head of construction investment association says Kabariti sympathises with problems for investors from new income tax regulations on property investments.
- Jordan details 24 projects to potential international investors at Cairo conference.
